<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-author">Author</button></h2><div id="work-acc-author" class="accordion-collapse collapse show"><div class="accordion-body"><p class="mb-0 work-author"><a href="../poets/padmagupta.html">Padmagupta</a></p></div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The poem tells the story of King Sindhu, a ruler known for his generosity and hospitality towards scholars and poets. When Padmagupta, a poet and scholar, comes to the Kingdom seeking refuge from his enemies, King Sindhu welcomes him with open arms and offers him shelter in his palace.<br>In gratitude, Padmagupta composes the Navasāhasāṃkacarita, a poem consisting of nine cantos that praises King Sindhu's virtues and achievements. The poem is characterized by vivid descriptions of nature, social customs of ancient India, and adventures of its hero, King Sindhu.<br>Throughout the poem, Padmagupta extols the virtues of King Sindhu, depicting him as a just and righteous ruler who cares for his subjects and treats guests with kindness and respect. The poem also includes philosophical and moral teachings, as well as depictions of love and romance.<br>In summary, Navasāhasāṃkacarita is a work of epic poetry that celebrates the virtues of King Sindhu, his hospitality and generosity towards scholars and poets, as well as the culture and society of ancient India.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Brief overview of the contents of Navasāhasāṃkacarita:<br><br>Canto 1: The first canto introduces King Sindhu and his Kingdom, which is depicted as prosperous and peaceful. The canto also introduces the poet Padmagupta and his arrival in the kingdom seeking refuge.<br><br>Canto 2: The second canto describes King Sindhu's generosity and hospitality towards Padmagupta. The canto also praises the beauty and richness of the natural world.<br><br>Canto 3: The third canto describes King Sindhu's love for his queen, his devotion to his subjects, and his reputation as a just and virtuous ruler.<br><br>Canto 4: The fourth canto narrates King Sindhu's adventures, including his battles against enemies, his travels to distant lands, and his encounters with various creatures and beings.<br><br>Canto 5: The fifth canto describes King Sindhu's victory over his enemies and his return to his Kingdom, where he is welcomed by his people and his queen.<br><br>Canto 6: The sixth canto describes King Sindhu's court and the various scholars and poets who visit him. The canto also praises the beauty and richness of Sanskrit language and literature.<br><br>Canto 7: The seventh canto narrates the story of Śaśiprabhā, a Princess whom King Sindhu falls in love with. The canto describes their courtship and eventual marriage.<br><br>Canto 8: The eighth canto describes King Sindhu's virtues, including his devotion to dharma (righteousness) and his compassion towards all living beings.<br><br>Canto 9: The ninth canto concludes the poem with a prayer to the divine powers and a praise of King Sindhu's virtues and achievements.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">1\) Praise of hospitality and generosity: The poem's central theme is the praise of King Sindhu's hospitality and generosity towards scholars and poets. This theme is unique in that it celebrates the importance of treating guests with respect and kindness, a value that was highly regarded in ancient Indian society.<br>2) Vivid descriptions of nature: The poem is known for its vivid descriptions of the natural world, including flora and fauna, mountains and rivers, and the changing seasons. These descriptions are considered unique for their rich imagery and attention to detail.<br>3) Inclusion of philosophical and moral teachings: The poem includes philosophical and moral teachings, including discussions of dharma (righteousness), karma (action), and mokṣa (liberation). These teachings are presented in a poetic and accessible manner, making them easy for readers to understand and appreciate.<br>4) Depictions of love and romance: The poem includes depictions of love and romance, particularly in the story of King Sindhu and Padmāvatī. These depictions are notable for their sensitivity and emotional depth.<br>5) Celebration of Sanskrit language and literature: The poem celebrates the beauty and richness of the Sanskrit language and its literary tradition. It includes references to various Sanskrit texts and authors, as well as discussions of the importance of poetry and scholarship in ancient Indian society.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Navasāhasāṃkacarita is considered a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature for several reasons:<br>Unique poetic style: The poem's unique poetic style, which includes vivid descriptions of nature, philosophical and moral teachings, and depictions of love and romance, was innovative for its time and influenced later Sanskrit poets.<br>Celebration of hospitality and generosity: The poem's celebration of hospitality and generosity towards scholars and poets helped to reinforce the value of treating guests with respect and kindness in ancient Indian society.<br>Cultural and historical significance: The poem provides valuable insights into the culture and history of ancient India, including its literature, philosophy, and social customs.<br>Influence on later literature: The poem's themes and motifs have been echoed in later works of Sanskrit literature, demonstrating its enduring influence on the literary tradition.<br><br>Navasāhasāṃkacarita is a Sanskrit epic poem written by the 11th-century Indian poet Padmagupta, which tells the story of King Sindhu and his 900 elephants. The poem is written in the Mahākāvya style and explores themes such as love, hospitality, nature, and interconnectedness. It is known for its rich and evocative language, vivid descriptions of nature, and innovative use of metaphor and symbolism. Navasāhasāṃkacarita has been highly influential in Indian literature and culture, and is considered one of the finest examples of Sanskrit literature.</div></div></div>
